metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:training_positions: Descriptive position-weighted training statistics from at most ten batches, requiring nonzero sequence, positive and negative IDs. No independent-user inference.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-negative training score; scale dependent.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-rank tenth percentile of training margins.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of valid training margins below zero.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of valid training margins below 0.5; this threshold is scale dependent.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pairwise_accuracy: P(positive score > negative score) + 0.5 P(tie), conditional on sampled negative difficulty; invariant to strictly increasing score transformations.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_angular_alignmen: (Mean off-diagonal cosine + 1)/2; approximately 0.5 means zero mean cosine. Not a ranking-quality or semantic-diversity metric.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:representations: Centered covariance eigenvalues for raw and unit-normalized vectors; total variance, largest eigenvalue share and exp(-sum(p log p)), where p is covariance eigenvalue mass. This is not RankMe. Zero variance has null effective rank.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:structure: Inspection of actual NextItNet residual blocks, temporal convolutions, positionwise norms, biases, explicit causal padding and masks. Reachability is conditional on this recognized graph and absence of unrecognized operations.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:checks: Feature comparisons in eval mode: atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5; report maximum absolute difference. Width checks retain item content but may change absolute positions.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:training_endpoint_interven: Fixed positive/negative endpoint pair, largest nonzero index, descriptive loader-row margin changes; rows are not identified independent users.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:user_score_sensitivity: Identified public training users, fixed 99 training-observed unseen candidates per user. Mean absolute score change and signed mean score change; no relevance labels, HR or target ranks.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:temporal_geometry: Identified-user strengths 0.25 and 0.5 use k=max(1,floor(fraction*original_nonpadding_length)), before baseline truncation. Interventions are unavailable when retained history cannot support the requested size or preserve the newest k items. Loader-row probes use their observed nonpadding lengths because full histories are unidentified. Deletions compact and left-pad; replacements preserve positions; shuffles preserve identities and multiplicities. Unchanged draws are excluded and counted, so shuffle estimates condition on changed draws.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:user_intervals: Pointwise 95% percentile intervals from 2000 seed-42 user bootstrap resamples. Each complete paired vector is resampled together within the current category and original-length stratum. Conditional on fitted model, fixed users/candidates; excludes training-seed, candidate-sampling and adaptive-search uncertainty. Exploratory, no p-values.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:missingness: Unavailable observations are null with reasons, never zero-effect evidence. Cross-category macro estimates require all four categories.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:intact_user_endpoint_repre: Raw and unit-normalized covariance statistics and norm quantiles for one intact final-nonpadding feature per identified training user eligible for the fixed-candidate sensitivity probe. Loader endpoint statistics remain separate and may contain repeated users.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:paired_contrasts: Within-user difference between each named method and the first method in its declared comparison family, computed on common eligible users. Bootstrap intervals resample each complete paired vector together. These are score-sensitivity contrasts, not ranking improvements.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:candidate_depth_audit: In-sample exploratory training-prefix audit; no validation labels. Up to 200 uniformly sampled eligible users without replacement, sorted before selection; seed 42 plus declared category index and stable hashed user ID for ten independent candidate repetitions. Unknown category uses index 4 and must not be treated as a named category macro report. Each target is the final permitted training interaction; its cutoff is a zero-based training index, and it may have been optimized during fitting. Prefixes are left-padded/truncated to model.maxlen and read at the largest nonzero index. The catalog contains only mapped training-observed items. Negative pools exclude every full training-history item, including target; this is retrospective hindsight rather than a prospective exclusion policy. Repeated targets are recorded before exclusion. Ten uniform ordered samples without replacement share nested prefixes of 99/499/999 negatives. Missing depths are unavailable, with counts in user-repetition-depth units. Ties favor ascending item ID. Rank includes the positive; hit means rank<=10. Margin subtracts the tenth largest negative score and is scale dependent. Nested ranks cannot improve with depth; declining hit rates alone imply nothing about generalization. Users receive equal weight; depth-specific populations may differ. Paired comparisons use common eligible users and 2000 seed-42 user-cluster bootstrap resamples conditional on candidate repetition zero. Intervals exclude training seed, adaptive search and candidate-resampling uncertainty. Repetition SD is computed across ten category-level summaries; SD/sqrt(10) is solely Monte Carlo error of their average, with model and users fixed. Repetitions are never independent users. Frequency bands use all valid permitted training interactions, descending frequency then ascending item ID: first ceil(20%) head, next through ceil(50%) middle, remainder tail. Length bins use prefixes before truncation. At most 50 randomly selected audit users have exact full-eligible-pool ranks; scores stream in chunks<=4096 and retain only the top ten negative items. N is eligible negative count and M counts negatives preceding the target. Conditional expected hit is hypergeom.cdf(9,N,M,m); expected rank is 1+m*M/N, applicable only to declared uniform sampling and tie order. Expected/observed residuals measure sampling variability, not generalization. Recommendation popularity and catalog coverage describe top-ten scores on these same restricted negative pools, excluding known training items and the target; they are not unrestricted-catalog recommendation quality. Existing controlled shuffle/truncation probes remain descriptive controls. Only one category is measured here; four-category macro summaries require all four reports and equal category weights. No auxiliary scorer or model is fitted.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:diagnostic_elapsed_seconds: Wall-clock seconds for all probes, including exact eligible-pool scoring and final CUDA synchronization; prior queued CUDA work is excluded by synchronizing before timing. Diagnostic execution consumes the shared experiment budget.
